# YM41: 大宫门 Da Gongmen, "The Great Palace Gate"

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM41` · Page: `/scenes/#YM41` · Row: `research/buildings/YM41-da-gongmen/`

## What it was

大宫门 Da Gongmen, the Great Palace Gate, is the south front of the garden and the start of the official axis to 正大光明 (S05 j80:7b-9a, E2101). From the spirit wall (Malone: 137 ft long, about 15 ft high, E2114; the dig report gives 41.6 m, 204.8 m south of the gate, S102 E1017) the carriage road ran north between the two halves of the Front Lake to the five-bay gate hall, with five-bay court offices left and right before it (S05 j80:7b-8b). Behind the court offices stood the duty rooms of the boards and the eight banners, east and west by name, the silver vault and 南书房 in the east lane and the 造办处 workshop and dispensary in the south-west (j80:8b-9a). The gate carried Yongzheng's plaque 圆明园 (j80:1b; Malone says Kangxi's: question row). The three courts from the gate to the hall measure 370 m north-south and 310 m between the 如意门 gates by the dig report (E1017). Amherst reached the gate at daybreak in 1816 and left without an audience (S02, E2112). On 6 October 1860 French troops with a British cavalry brigade arrived at seven in the evening, and a few eunuchs defended the gate (S02 from Cordier, E2110); the looting followed on 7-8 October. The dig of the late 2010s found the gate hall, the east and west wing gates, the 金水桥 and the canal (S132, E2120).

From the inventory row: **built** 雍正三年 1725 区域 (S42); **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S42, S01, S102).

### The garden around it

Wolseley saw ponds with lilies and lotus at the edges along the causeway, a temple under tall trees at its end, and gate courts enclosed on three sides by carved and painted guard-houses whose sills stood 2-3 ft above the pavement with granite ramps (S240, E2108; pp.231-232, E2109). Lucy describes a small lake and wood on the left of the approach and the great gate at the back of a vast half circle (S247, E2103). A Daoguang-era Manchu account has yellow earth spread on the road and side streets curtained as the emperor rode by (S02 from 鸿雪因缘图记, E2116).

## What survives today

The 大宫门 area was dug by the 北京市文物研究所 in at least two phases (a 2016 request of the 北京市文物局 says the second was finished, per a search extract of S154; results announced January 2019): gate hall, east and west wing gates, the 金水桥 and the river (S132; S154). The gate hall stood on a base 21.57 x 11.33 m, 0.77 m high; the screen wall is 41.6 m long and 204.8 m south of the gate terrace (S102 as recorded in E1017). The 12-page brief (S154) is locked.

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.

## Gaps and wishlist

No plan of the 大宫门 itself found. The wall plans 样098-3 (1811-27) and 样1704 write wall lengths (E0530, E0529); the 初编 section 正大光明 pp.13-31 (E1015) may include the gate.

- **Q28. 1860 and after, for the site's text.** Main account: 6 Oct French marines at the outer gate of 大宫门, 7–8 Oct looting, 18–19 Oct burning ordered by Elgin and done by 3500 British troops under Michel, French refused (S02 pp.179–188). S06 reports 王闿运 and 李慈铭 blaming local looters first: needs a stronger source befor

Take S05 for the 1780s; whether a plaque m
